finalText:
Two things usually cause this.

First, by default React re-renders every child whenever the parent re-renders, no matter what the props are. Wrapping the child in `React.memo` tells React to skip it when the props haven't changed.

Second, even with `React.memo`, "same props" often isn't actually true. If you pass an inline function, object, or array (like `onClick={() => ...}` or `style={{color: 'red'}}`), a brand new one gets built on every render. It looks the same but React sees it as a different value. Fixing this usually means wrapping the function in `useCallback` and the object or array in `useMemo`, so the same one gets reused across renders.

If it's still re-rendering after both of those, check whether the child reads from a Context — a Context value changing will re-render every component reading it, memo or not.
